title: Banding induced by standard LTX 2.5 VAE Decode

latest.raw:
Trying to set up a 10 bit workflow I discovered banding in highly saturated areas of my videos.
So I set up a simple test after reading that setting the VAE  encode and decode to float32 could help.

[1]. Just load a video with a VHS-Loader and directly save it
[2]. Load a video, convert it to latent with the standard encoder, decode it with the standard decoder and save it . (both the standard [2.1] bf16 and the [2.2] conv version)
[3]. replace the VAE Encode and Decode with the ANDRO nodes set to float32

[1| looks just fine
[2.1] serious banding
[2.2]much less banding, but in my actual production workflow, the convolutional version introduces a lot of noise
[3] no difference to the stock nodes

Can anyone point me to a solution for using the newer standard 2.5 VAE without introducing as much banding? Or a starting point for further reading?

Workflow in Comfy 
Stock LTX 2.5 VAEs https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.5/tree/main/vae



![Screenshot 2026-10-15 at 21.22.26](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/69a87db1179a33ddcc7afdab/lvD350fZcynYyJFK8TnE9.png)

latest.raw:
Technically the force float32 node is there to solve just this, just connect it to the vae before encode/decode nodes

![image](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/6354d6c25eac2d2efa7c15ca/v3-il2hor5noYTCai-RNN.png)

Unless you already start comfyui with the flag that ensures vae runs at fp32 the above node (or equivalent) is necessary, don't download the already bf16 var, just use the one in the checkpoint.

latest.raw: @Lordenpropf as I mentioned above, you must pull the full precision fp32 vae from the checkpoint, you're using a bf16 (already downsized precision file), no amount of "forcing" will give it more precision, it's "baked"  in bf16 already so you will always have the banding if you use that bf16 safetensors file.

latest.raw:
@oumoumad Same here — I couldn't find an fp32 video VAE anywhere either. I checked the safetensors headers directly:

- LTX-2.5/vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-bf16.safetensors → all 396 tensors BF16
- LTX-2.5/vae/ltx-2.5-video-vae-conv-bf16.safetensors → all BF16
- LTX-2.5-Pre-Trained/ltx-2.5-22b-pt-bf16.safetensors → vae.* tensors (396) are all BF16, identical to the standalone file
- The 42GB dev/distilled transformer files in diffusion_models/ don't contain a VAE at all

So as far as I can tell, there's no checkpoint with an fp32 VAE to pull from. Could you point us to it, or release a separate fp32 video VAE? Thanks!

latest.raw:
We found the cause. The VHS Video Combine node quietly converts frames to 8-bit before writing ProRes, so your 10-bit files actually contain 8-bit data. On the passthrough you don't notice, because the grain hides the 8-bit steps. The VAE removes most of the grain, so the steps become visible, and grading makes them obvious. When we saved the same VAE output in true 10-bit or 16-bit (FFV1, EXR, or ComfyUI's core Create Video at 10-bit), there was no visible banding, even after strong contrast.

![image](https://cdn-uploads.huggingface.co/production/uploads/6a29409b551a1fe1e7dfdcfe/BXhbGlQ0hlvF-2wh55PqP.png)
